strings.title: Scale on a Map
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: A map scale is a rate: 1 cm on the map is 25 km on the ground. Scale up to find real distances, or back down to find map distances.
strings.keywords: scale, map, centimetres, kilometres, rate, ratio
watchFor: Adding 25 instead of multiplying (4 cm = 29 km): ask "Is every centimetre worth 25 km?"
Going the wrong way for map distance (150 × 25): ask "Is the map distance bigger or smaller than the real one?"
Decimal centimetres: ask "What's half a centimetre worth? A tenth?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "How is a map scale like a unit rate?" Land: 1 cm stands for 25 km, so multiply map centimetres by 25 for kilometres, and divide kilometres by 25 to get centimetres.

problems.notes: Context: "On a map, 1 cm represents 25 km." Look for: 4 × 25. Ask: "How far is 4 cm?" Word choice: "represents", "scale". Model: ratio cm:km, 1:25, 4:100

responses.tip: Added 3 to both. Ask: is every centimetre worth 25 km?

problems.notes: Look for: 2 cm = 50, 0.4 cm = 10. Ask: "What's 0.4 cm worth?" Model: ratio cm:km, 1:25, 2:50, 0.4:10, 2.4:60
Look for: 150 ÷ 25. Ask: "Is the map distance bigger or smaller?" Model: ratio cm:km, 1:25, 6:150

responses.tip: Ask: would 3750 cm fit on a map?

problems.notes: Look for: 6 tenths of 25. Ask: "What's 0.1 cm worth?" Model: ratio cm:km, 1:25, 0.2:5, 0.6:15

responses.say: 0.2 cm is 5 km, so 0.6 cm is 15 km.

problems.notes: Look for: 1 cm = 25, 0.6 cm = 15. Ask: "How does the last one help?" Model: ratio cm:km, 1:25, 0.6:15, 1.6:40
Look for: 7 cm = 175, 0.2 cm = 5. Ask: "Which parts?" Model: ratio cm:km, 1:25, 7:175, 0.2:5, 7.2:180

strings.title: Converting Units with Rates
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: A unit conversion is a rate: 1 hour is 60 minutes, 1 inch is 2.54 cm. Use a ratio table to convert either way.
strings.keywords: convert, unit, rate, hours, minutes, inches, centimetres, ratio table
watchFor: Writing 2.5 hours as 2 h 50 min: ask "What is half an hour in minutes?"
Multiplying when converting to a bigger unit: ask "Should there be more hours or more minutes?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "How did you know whether to multiply or divide?" Land: converting to a smaller unit gives a bigger number (multiply); to a bigger unit gives a smaller number (divide). The ratio table keeps it straight.

problems.notes: Context: "A movie is 2.5 hours long. How many minutes?" Look for: 2 h = 120, half an hour = 30. Ask: "Is it 2 h 50 min?" Word choice: "convert". Model: ratio hours:minutes, 1:60, 2:120, 0.5:30, 2.5:150

responses.tip: Ask: how many minutes are in one hour?

problems.notes: Look for: 45 minutes is 3/4 of an hour. Ask: "What fraction of an hour?" Model: ratio hours:minutes, 1:60, 0.25:15, 0.75:45

responses.say: A quarter hour is 15 minutes, so 0.75 hours.

responses.tip: Ask: is 45 minutes almost half an hour or three quarters?

problems.notes: Look for: a fifth of 60. Ask: "What's 0.1 hours?" Model: ratio hours:minutes, 1:60, 0.1:6, 0.2:12

responses.say: 0.1 h is 6 min, so 0.2 h is 12 min.

responses.tip: Ask: is 0.2 of an hour the same as 20 minutes?

problems.notes: Context: "1 inch is 2.54 cm." Look for: ×10. Ask: "How many cm in 10 inches?" Model: ratio inches:cm, 1:2.54, 10:25.4
Look for: 10 in + 2 in = 25.4 + 5.08. Ask: "How long is a foot in cm?" Model: ratio inches:cm, 10:25.4, 2:5.08, 12:30.48

responses.tip: Ask: about how big should 12 × 2.5 be?

problems.notes: Context: "1 km is 1000 m. How many km is 250 m?" Look for: a quarter. Ask: "What fraction of 1000 is 250?" Model: ratio km:m, 1:1000, 0.25:250

strings.title: Comparing Mixtures
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: To compare two mixtures, make one part the same in both, or find what percent of each mixture is concentrate. Then the comparison is fair.
strings.keywords: concentrate, mixture, stronger, part to part, part to whole, percent, compare
watchFor: Comparing the differences (Mix B has 2 more cups of water than concentrate, Mix A only 1): ask "Does the difference tell you how strong it tastes?"
Mixing part-to-part and part-to-whole: ask "Is 2 out of 3, or 2 out of 5 cups?"
Thinking more concentrate always means stronger: ask "What about the water?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "Which mix is stronger, and how do you know?" Land: compare fairly by making the concentrate the same (6 cups in each) or by finding the percent of concentrate in the whole mixture.

problems.notes: Context: "Mix A: 2 cups orange concentrate for 3 cups water. Mix B: 3 cups concentrate for 5 cups water." Look for: ×3. Ask: "How much water with 6 cups of concentrate in Mix A?" Word choice: "concentrate", "stronger". Model: ratio concentrate:water, 2:3, 6:9
Look for: ×2. Ask: "Now compare: which has more water for the same concentrate?" Model: ratio concentrate:water, 3:5, 6:10

responses.say: Double Mix B: 6 concentrate, 10 water. B is weaker.
B is stronger, because it has 3 cups of concentrate.
responses.tip: Ask: B has more water too. Is it a fair comparison?

problems.notes: Look for: Mix A is 2 cups concentrate out of 5 cups total. Ask: "What percent of Mix A is concentrate?" Model: ratio concentrate:total, 2:5, 40:100

responses.tip: Used part to part (2 to 3). Ask: how many cups are in the whole mix?

problems.notes: Look for: Mix B is 3 out of 8 cups. Ask: "What's 1 out of 8 as a percent?" Model: ratio concentrate:total, 1:8, 3:24, 37.5:100
Context: "Mix C: 5 cups concentrate for 7 cups water." Look for: ×3. Ask: "Compare C with A: 15 concentrate each?" Model: ratio concentrate:water, 5:7, 15:21

responses.say: 15 concentrate needs 21 water in Mix C.
Mix A with 15 concentrate would be 22.5 water, so C is stronger.
responses.tip: Ask: why does less water mean stronger?

problems.notes: Context: "Mix D: 1 cup concentrate for 3 cups water." Look for: 1 out of 4 cups total. Ask: "Part to whole: 1 out of how many?" Model: ratio concentrate:total, 1:4, 25:100

responses.say: 1 out of 4 cups is 25%, the weakest.

responses.tip: Part to part again. Ask: how many cups in the whole mix?

strings.connection: Day 8: Percent as a Rate per 100

strings.title: Rates with Parts of an Hour
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: When a rate is given for part of an hour (2 km in half an hour), scale up to 1 hour to get the speed, then use it for other times.
strings.keywords: speed, km per hour, part of an hour, half, quarter, scale up
watchFor: Treating the given distance as the hourly speed (2 km in 1/2 h = 2 km/h): ask "How far in a whole hour?"
Dividing instead of multiplying (2 ÷ 2 = 1): ask "Is a whole hour longer or shorter than half an hour?"
Stuck with 15 minutes: ask "How many quarter hours in an hour?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "How did you get to a whole hour each time?" Land: if you know a part of an hour, multiply up: ×2 for a half, ×4 for a quarter, ×(4/3) for three quarters. That's the speed per hour.

problems.notes: Context: "A hiker walks 2 km in half an hour." Look for: double. Ask: "How far in a whole hour?" Word choice: "km per hour". Model: doubleline hours:km, 0:0, 0.5:2, 1:4

responses.tip: Ask: is a whole hour longer or shorter than half an hour?

problems.notes: Look for: 2 h = 8 km, half hour = 2 km. Ask: "How does 4 km/h help?" Model: doubleline hours:km, 0:0, 0.5:2, 2:8, 2.5:10
Context: "A cyclist goes 1.5 km in 15 minutes." Look for: ×4. Ask: "How many quarter hours in an hour?" Model: doubleline hours:km, 0:0, 0.25:1.5, 1:6

responses.tip: Added. Ask: what does 0.25 mean here?

problems.notes: Look for: three quarter hours: 3 × 1.5. Ask: "Is it more or less than 6?" Model: doubleline hours:km, 0:0, 0.25:1.5, 0.75:4.5, 1:6
Context: "A runner covers 3 km in 45 minutes." Look for: 1 km per 15 min, so 4 km per hour. Ask: "What's 15 minutes?" Model: doubleline hours:km, 0:0, 0.25:1, 0.75:3, 1:4

responses.say: 15 min is 1 km, so an hour is 4 km.

responses.tip: Multiplied. Ask: in a whole hour, more or less than 3 km?

problems.notes: Context: "A swimmer swims 6 km in 1.5 hours." Look for: ÷3. Ask: "How many half hours in 1.5 hours?" Model: doubleline hours:km, 0:0, 0.5:2, 1.5:6
